title: The Payroll Verification Trap
subject: URGENT: Verify Your Payroll Details Before 5 PM
scenario:
Dear Employee,

As part of the monthly payroll audit, employees must confirm their salary account details before 5 PM. The notice states that records not confirmed by the deadline will be excluded from this month's payment file.

Use the verification portal below. The message says replies are not monitored.

Regards,
Human Resources
email_note: Compare the sender domain with the displayed link and its actual destination. Consider the payroll deadline and the instruction not to reply.
options: The sender's display name matches a department, and the displayed URL contains the company name, so the request can be treated as authentic unless the browser raises a warning.
The deadline is the main concern; if the employee opens the link in a private browser window and avoids saving the password, the verification process is sufficiently safe.

The sender domain is not the company's domain, the destination resolves to a separate lookalike domain, and the salary-processing threat is being used to rush employees into submitting sensitive information.
The message may be legitimate because payroll teams perform periodic audits; the employee should complete the form but contact HR afterward if any account details appear incorrect.
explanation: The sender domain and actual destination are not the official company domain. The displayed link is misleading, and the salary threat creates urgency. Verify payroll requests using a contact method already known to be genuine.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.

title: The Microsoft Sign-in Warning
subject: Your Microsoft 365 Account Will Be Suspended
scenario:
Dear User,

Our identity monitoring platform has detected an unfamiliar sign-in. Your Microsoft 365 access will be restricted in 30 minutes unless you complete the security confirmation below.

Sign in to retain access to company email, shared files and scheduled meetings.

IT Support Team
email_note: Inspect the full sender address and actual destination. A familiar product name or logo does not authenticate a message.
options: The external sender domain, artificial 30-minute deadline and unrelated sign-in destination form a credential-harvesting pattern; the alert should be verified through the company's established IT channel.
A real identity alert can contain a short response window, so the employee should use the displayed Microsoft address and proceed if the page looks visually consistent with the normal sign-in screen.
The sender's failure to include the employee's name is the decisive indicator; if the employee's name is added in a follow-up message, the warning can be treated as genuine.
The message should be forwarded to colleagues to check whether they received the same warning, and the first employee to confirm it can safely complete the sign-in.
explanation: The sender is external, the deadline is designed to create panic, and the actual link is not Microsoft's sign-in domain. Do not enter credentials through the link; report and verify independently.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.

title: The Unexpected QR Code
subject: Mandatory MFA Re-registration Required
scenario:
Dear Employee,

We are migrating the multi-factor authentication service. Scan the attached QR code to reconnect your company account before close of business.

If the QR code fails, reply with your current one-time authentication code so that support can complete activation manually.

Regards,
IT Support
email_note: The sender address appears familiar. Evaluate the requested action itself, not only the sender identity.
options: Because the sender uses the company domain, the QR code can be scanned on a work phone; only the request to send the code by email should be ignored.
The QR code should be scanned after checking that the attachment is a PNG file, because image files cannot execute programs in the same way as office documents.
The request is acceptable if the employee changes their password immediately after scanning, since that would invalidate any credentials captured during the process.

An unexpected QR code may lead to an attacker-controlled authentication page, and disclosing a one-time code could let another person complete a login; confirm the migration with IT using a trusted channel.
explanation: A QR code can conceal a phishing URL, and one-time codes must never be shared. A familiar sender address alone does not prove that the account or message is safe.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.

title: The Courier Delivery Document
subject: Failed Office Delivery – Action Required
scenario:
Dear Recipient,

A shipment addressed to your office could not be delivered because the recipient details were incomplete. Open the attached document to confirm the delivery address and select a new delivery slot.

The shipment will be returned if no action is recorded within 24 hours.

Delivery Operations
email_note: Review the unexpected delivery claim, sender identity and attachment type before deciding what to do.
options: The workbook is acceptable if opened in protected view, because that feature prevents all malicious activity until the user explicitly enables editing.

The sender is not independently verified, the employee may not be expecting a shipment, and the macro-enabled workbook could run code; verify the parcel with the carrier through its known website or phone number.
The attachment should be uploaded to a public malware-scanning website first; if the service reports no detection, the employee can safely enable its macros.
The delivery deadline is the only meaningful concern; if the employee is expecting any office parcel, the attachment can be opened to identify the shipment.
explanation: An unexpected delivery message from an unverified sender combined with a macro-enabled attachment is high risk. Verify the shipment independently and do not enable macros.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.

title: The CEO's Confidential Request
subject: Confidential – Immediate Assistance Required
scenario:
Hello,

I am in an external meeting and cannot take calls. Please purchase gift cards for a client appreciation activity using your personal payment method. Email me the redemption codes and I will arrange reimbursement.

Keep this confidential until the client announcement.

Regards,
Managing Director
email_note: Consider the payment method, the request for redemption codes, the secrecy instruction and the sender's identity.
options: The employee should buy the cards only after receiving a written reimbursement promise, because the financial risk is then documented even if the sender cannot be reached.
The request can be processed if the gift-card value stays below the employee's normal expense limit and the receipt is submitted through the expense system.

The request combines an unverified executive identity, personal payment, transfer of redeemable codes and secrecy; independently contact the executive through a known number and follow the company's purchasing process.
The employee should reply asking for the client's name and event details; a convincing business explanation would provide enough context to proceed.
explanation: This is a classic executive impersonation and gift-card scam. Never send redemption codes or make personal payments based on an unverified urgent request.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.

title: The Shared Project Document
subject: A Document Has Been Shared With You
scenario:
Hello,

A colleague has shared the revised project budget. The document must be reviewed before tomorrow's meeting. Sign in with your company credentials using the access portal below.

The share will expire at the end of today.

Project Collaboration Team
email_note: Check the sender, link destination and whether the share can be confirmed from the collaboration platform directly.
options: The sender is an unfamiliar external address, the real destination differs from the displayed Office URL, and the expiry warning pressures the recipient; check the document directly in the approved collaboration service.
A document-sharing alert is expected in most workplaces, so the employee should sign in if the page uses the same colours and logo as the company's normal collaboration portal.
The employee can safely open the link on a mobile device instead of a work computer, because credential theft is less likely when the device is not connected to the office network.
The correct response is to reply to the sender requesting access permissions; replying does not expose credentials, so there is no need to verify the sender first.
explanation: Fake sharing notifications commonly steal credentials. The sender and actual destination are untrusted, and the expiry message adds pressure. Open the approved platform independently and check there.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.

title: The Vendor Bank Account Change
subject: Important: Updated Bank Details for Future Payments
scenario:
Dear Accounts Team,

We have changed our banking partner. Please update the beneficiary details in the attached document before processing invoice INV-7316. Do not use the previous account after today, as the old account is being closed.

Regards,
ABC Industrial Supplies
email_note: A genuine supplier can change bank accounts. The control question is how the change is authenticated before money is transferred.
options: Compare the beneficiary name and invoice amount with the purchase order; if both match, the bank-account change is sufficiently supported for payment.

Treat the request as a potential business-email-compromise attempt: freeze the change and verify it using a previously registered supplier contact number, then follow the required dual-approval process.
Ask the sender to provide a cancelled cheque or bank letter by replying to the same email thread, then update the details if the document appears consistent.
Make a small test transfer to the new account and wait for the supplier to acknowledge it before sending the remaining invoice amount.
explanation: A compromised supplier mailbox or impersonator can submit convincing bank-change documents. Verify through a previously trusted contact route and retain the required approval evidence before changing payment details.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.

title: The Duplicate Invoice Pressure
subject: Urgent: Pending Invoice – Second Payment Required
scenario:
Dear Accounts Team,

The supplier says payment for invoice INV-2481 has not arrived. They have requested another transfer today to prevent a delivery suspension. Please process the attached copy now; Finance will reconcile the earlier transaction later.

Regards,
Finance Coordination
email_note: The sender appears internal. Focus on the transaction history, invoice controls and request to defer reconciliation.
options: Ask the supplier to confirm the outstanding amount by replying to the existing thread, then pay if the supplier repeats the request and the delivery deadline is documented.
Process the second payment but flag both transactions for month-end review, because a temporary duplicate payment can be reversed after the supplier confirms receipt.
Check whether the PDF has a new issue date and approval stamp; if the document is current, the duplicate payment can proceed while the earlier transfer is investigated.

Do not release a second payment until the first transaction is traced and reconciled against bank confirmation, ledger entries and supplier records; escalate any mismatch through the approved finance workflow.
explanation: A second payment should never be released simply because of urgency. Reconcile the first payment and verify the supplier's claim before taking action.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.

title: The Purchase Order Approval Shortcut
subject: Management Approved – Release Purchase Order Immediately
scenario:
Hello Team,

Management has verbally approved the attached purchase order for urgent equipment. The workflow is delayed, so release the order directly to the supplier. The formal approval document will be uploaded next week.

Please do not hold the order for the usual system confirmation.

Regards,
Procurement Operations
email_note: An internal sender can still make an improper request. Evaluate the control being bypassed and the evidence of authorization.
options: Do not release the purchase order until the required approval is recorded in the authorized system; independently confirm the verbal instruction and escalate pressure to bypass the control.
Proceed if the sender is listed in the procurement directory and the purchase value is within the department's usual spending range.
Ask the supplier to begin preparing the equipment but delay the invoice until the formal approval document is uploaded next week.
Accept a manager's confirmation in a chat message as a temporary substitute, provided the procurement team saves a screenshot for the audit file.
explanation: A request to bypass the approval workflow is a control failure even if it appears to come from an internal team. Authorization must be independently verified and recorded before commitment.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.

title: The Employee Salary Account Update
subject: Employee Bank Account Update – Process Before Payroll Closure
scenario:
Dear Payroll Team,

An employee has requested a change to their salary account. The new details are attached. The employee is currently unavailable, but payroll closes today. Please update the record now to avoid delaying the salary run.

Regards,
Payroll Administration
email_note: Check the sender domain, employee identity verification and whether the request follows the approved payroll change procedure.
options: Accept the spreadsheet if it includes the employee's name, employee number and a bank proof document, then ask the employee to confirm the change after payroll closes.
Call the phone number included in the email signature and proceed if the person answering can state the employee's department and reporting manager.
Reject the unverified change for now and confirm the employee's identity and request through the approved HR/payroll process using contact details already on record.
Update the account but place the record on a temporary hold, because payroll can reverse the change if the employee reports an issue later.
explanation: Payroll diversion fraud attempts to redirect salaries. Verify identity and bank changes through the established process and trusted contact information already on file.
evidence_caption: Training simulation — fictional example. Do not use real credentials, payment details or links.
